name: Side Cutters (Diagonal Cutters)
tagline: Snip conductors cleanly at the jaws' edge — the workhorse for trimming to length at a terminal.
parts: Diagonal cutting edges — shear against each other
Pivot joint — transfers grip pressure into shear
Spring return — opens the jaws for rapid repeat cuts
Beaded insulation grips — rated to a working voltage
safety: Use the cutting edge only for the conductor sizes stamped on the tool. Cutting armour or steel with a copper cutter blunts it — and an unblunted cutter can slip onto your fingers.

points.label: Diagonal cutting edges
points.detail:
The jaws meet at an angle and slice by shear — one blade rides just past the other. This shearing action gives a clean square cut on copper up to the stamped capacity (often ~2.5–4 mm²).

Cut conductors square at the stripped length; a diagonal nick starts a future break under vibration.

points.label: Pivot joint
points.detail: A precision rivet lets the two blades rotate the exact amount needed for shear. Any play here makes the tool chew instead of cut — keep it clean and one-drop-oiled.

points.label: Spring return
points.detail: An external (or internal) spring pushes the jaws back open after each squeeze, so you can make dozens of cuts without re-opening by hand.

points.label: Beaded insulation grips
points.detail: The insulated handles are rated to a working voltage (check the marking; 1000 V is common). The raised 'beads' improve grip when your hands are oily.
